newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore, British navies sign cooperation pact.
newsitem.headline: Singapore, British navies sign cooperation pact.

text.p: Britain and Singapore signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) on Friday aimed at improving cooperation between their two navies. Signed at a ceremony on board British aircraft carrier Illustrious in Singapore, the MOU will increase training exchanges, joint exercises and visits between personnel, said Singapore Navy chief Rear Admiral Richard Lim.
"We are pleased that this has come about because it formalises the very strong relations between the two countries' navies," Lim told reporters.
Rear Admiral Alan West, commander of a 20-vessel British naval task force visiting Southeast Asia, said the pact showed Britain's commitment to stability in the region.
"It will give us the opportunity to cooperate more in future," West told reporters.

The British Task Force, known as Ocean Wave 97, will take part in the "Flying Fish" naval exercise in the South China Sea being organised by Britain, Australia, Malaysia, New Zealand and Singapore later in April.
Flying Fish will be the largest military exercise in the region for more than 20 years, Britian's Ministry of Defence said in a statement.
